headline: Congress required the Department of Veterans Affairs to test online and app-based appointment scheduling for veterans and to certify that its scheduling systems meet set standards.
what_it_does: The law directs the VA to run an 18-month pilot in at least three Veterans Integrated Service Networks, where veterans can book, confirm, change, and cancel VA medical appointments online or through a mobile app. The VA must try to hire contractors through competitive bidding for a self-scheduling system with features such as real-time availability, reposting cancelled slots, reminders for follow-up visits, and round-the-clock use. An outside nonprofit with health IT expertise must check that these systems have the required features, the GAO must review those checks, and the VA must certify compliance by December 31, 2017, with rules for replacing noncompliant systems.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who receive care through the VA health system
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to schedule and manage appointments online or by mobile app in the pilot locations, and the VA must use systems meeting the listed features.

who_it_affects.group: VA medical facilities and staff in the pilot networks
who_it_affects.how: They must take part in a pilot that uses online self-scheduling and may need to connect scheduling tools to existing VA health records systems.
Companies with commercially available, off-the-shelf online scheduling systems may compete for the VA contract.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 16, 2016; the VA must certify its systems by December 31, 2017, and the 18-month pilot runs after the VA sets it up.
